summary: Ramon N. Prats is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught Antonio Terrone and held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).
Randall Studstill works in religious studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Richard Payne and also studied under Steven D. Goodman.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at UC Berkeley (1983–1990) under James A. Matisoff (~1986–1990). He was a professor at City University of Hong Kong (~1996–2004) and held a post at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai (2021).

Rangama Chandawimala works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliya Anuruddha, and studied with Attaragama Gnanawimala. He is an associate professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche, 11th Tai Situpa Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and the 1st Beru Khyentse Rinpoche, and taught numerous students.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1948–1955) and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranu Kunwar is a PhD student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held an appointment as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (~1821–1824). He taught Georg Bühler.

Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) was a philosopher who studied at the Moscow Conservatory (~1867–1872), Heidelberg University (~1874–1878), and the University of Jena (~1878–1881). He held a post at the University of Tokyo from 1893.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Fergusson College under Ramchandra Dattatrya Ranade, he also studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinavijaya, later serving as professor at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1940).

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, he held librarian and professorial posts at the University of Copenhagen between 1814 and 1832.

Ratna Basu is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn in 1989. Attested in 2026, she holds a post as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society.
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and succeeded him in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Boise State University and the University of Oxford (DPhil 2000–2004), later becoming the Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State University (~2013).

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Lucknow, ASI Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He served in state archaeology departments and rose to Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1985–2004).

Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University. He was a physics professor (1945–1986) and director at Chulalongkorn University, and a fellow of the Royal Institute of Thailand (~1986–2017).

Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indology scholar who studied under Martin Haug (~1860–1866). He served as a judge on the Bombay High Court, Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge University.
Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker, whom he succeeded as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center (~1986–1995).
Rebecca Hufen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she is a doctoral student under Dorji Wangchuck and a lector for Tibetan Studies at the University of Hamburg.
